response.sql: WITH grp AS (SELECT ordersmark AS order_ref, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), tot AS (SELECT SUM(exec_count) AS total_execs FROM grp), shares AS (SELECT g.order_ref, g.exec_count, CAST(g.exec_count AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / t.total_execs AS share FROM grp g CROSS JOIN tot t), diffs AS (SELECT s.order_ref, s.exec_count, s.share, s.share - AVG(s.share) OVER () AS share_diff FROM shares s), ranked AS (SELECT d.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY d.share_diff DESC NULLS LAST) AS diff_rank FROM diffs d) SELECT order_ref, exec_count, share, share_diff FROM ranked WHERE diff_rank <= 10 ORDER BY share_diff DESC NULLS LAST

assumptions.assumption: The database is PostgreSQL-compatible (the schema uses PostgreSQL-style types and constraints), so NULLS LAST and DOUBLE PRECISION are valid.
Executions with a NULL ordersmark form one group that is returned as a row with a NULL order reference, and the average share is the unweighted mean over all groups, including that NULL group.
Share is the exact quotient of the group's execution count by the total execution count, with no rounding. Because the shares sum to 1, the average share equals 1 divided by the number of groups.
The rank is RANK() over share_diff in descending order, so tied rows share a rank and the next rank skips. Rows with rank 10 or better are kept, which can return more than 10 rows.

alternatives.interpretation: The average share is taken only over real order references, so the NULL-reference group is excluded from the average but still listed and ranked with its own difference.
alternatives.sql: WITH grp AS (SELECT ordersmark AS order_ref, COUNT(*) AS exec_count FROM orderexecutions GROUP BY ordersmark), tot AS (SELECT SUM(exec_count) AS total_execs FROM grp), shares AS (SELECT g.order_ref, g.exec_count, CAST(g.exec_count AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / t.total_execs AS share FROM grp g CROSS JOIN tot t), diffs AS (SELECT s.order_ref, s.exec_count, s.share, s.share - AVG(s.share) FILTER (WHERE s.order_ref IS NOT NULL) OVER () AS share_diff FROM shares s), ranked AS (SELECT d.*, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY d.share_diff DESC NULLS LAST) AS diff_rank FROM diffs d) SELECT order_ref, exec_count, share, share_diff FROM ranked WHERE diff_rank <= 10 ORDER BY share_diff DESC NULLS LAST
